questions.q: In what direction does a supplier refund move money, compared to a standard payment?
options: The same direction -- from the organization to the supplier
The opposite direction -- from the supplier back to the organization
It does not involve money movement at all
It moves money between two of the organization's own bank accounts
questions.explain: A supplier refund is money the supplier sends back to the organization, the reverse of a normal outbound payment.

questions.q: Which of these would typically create a refundable credit balance?
options: A prepayment left unapplied after the related work was cancelled
A standard invoice that was just validated
A purchase order that was approved but not yet invoiced
A quick payment issued today
questions.explain: An unused prepayment with no invoice to apply it against is a classic source of a refundable credit balance.

questions.q: How is a supplier refund recorded in Payables?
options: Through a Payment Process Request, like any outbound payment
By creating a new purchase order
Through a Record Refund action that applies the received money against the credit memo or prepayment
It cannot be recorded; it must be tracked manually outside the system
questions.explain: Record Refund captures what the supplier sent back and applies it against the specific credit/prepayment balance.

questions.q: In the BrightPath Consulting Group example, what happens to the $6,000 prepayment after the refund is recorded?
options: It remains an unapplied credit indefinitely
It is applied to a new, unrelated invoice
It is converted into a debit memo
The supplier's open credit balance returns to $0
questions.explain: Recording the refund against the prepayment closes out the credit, bringing the balance back to zero.

questions.q: What would happen if a refund received from a supplier were never recorded in Payables?
options: Nothing -- it has no effect on the books
The supplier's account would incorrectly continue showing an open credit balance
The original invoice would be automatically cancelled
The general ledger would close the period early
questions.explain: Failing to record the refund leaves the unapplied credit on the books, making it look like money is still owed when it has already been returned.
